prompt: Human: What type of soil is suitable for cactus?
response:
Cactus plants prefer well-drained soil that’s slightly acidic (pH around 6.0-6.8). Some soils can have a higher capacity to hold water, while other soils will retain a lot more minerals.  It’s important to note that while clay-based or sandy-based soils can have good drainage, both of those types of soils can also be heavy and retain too much moisture.  The best type of soil is one that is well-drained, not too dense, and matches the pH of the surrounding area.  Here are the top rated soils that work well with cactus plants:

- Cubbin clay: This is an Indian variety of volcanic rock with a clay-like texture. It has a fine aggregate structure that allows it to drain well. It is rich in nutrients and can handle quite a bit of lime and sulfur.  The key characteristic of this type of soil is the fine particles, which trap water and prevent it from escaping. However, since most cactus plants do not love acid soil, this can be an issue.  The average pH for the Indian Cubbin clay varies between 5.0 and 6.0. On the contrary, some cacti like to grow near the ocean in marine-rich soils with a low pH of around 6.0. Here’s a picture of a typical Indian Cubbin clay with the pH in the range of typical cactus plant roots:

- Mollisol: This is an alkaline clay soil and it’s fairly common in southwestern North America. It comes in various shades of brown or grey, and varies in texture from silty to coarse. It contains up to 14% sodium silicate. You can find Mollisol all across the southwestern US and Canada, especially in Arizona.
- Limestone: This is an alluvial type of soil. It occurs in coastal areas and it usually contains high amounts of calcium carbonate, which cacti dislike.
- Loamy clay: This is a sandy-to-stillly moist soil. It can range from clay to loamy. A good way to understand it is to consider the texture of the clay and the sand content. A soil made entirely of sand might contain too much water for cacti. Loamy soils have moderate drainage and are between clay and sandy soils. 
- Alluvial loam: This is a result of the deposition of sand and silt, and it’s a good combination of clay and loam. It is light and feels like sand most of the time, but can also have some clay or organic matter. In parts of the world, this type of soil is called eolian loam. The pH for alluvial loam varies from around 5.5-6.5.
- Silty loam: Similar in composition to loamy clay, this soil contains more organic matter. Like clay, it is either too wet or too dry for cactus to grow. With the exception of sandy loam soils in the Mediterranean region of Europe that may contain a lot of chloride, clay and loamy soils are all forms of loam soil. The pH for the best silty loam ranges between 5.5 and 6.2.

Now let’s say you want to grow a particular species of cactus, like the hairy cactus (Selenicereus spp.). Here’s a list of the best all-purpose cactus soils based on their performance when grown with this particular cactus:

- Indian Cubbin clay with sulfur, 5.0-6.0 pH, up to 28% calcium carbonate, 13% sodium silicate, up to 100 g/liter of potassium silicate: S. schmidgenii (Hairy)
- Indian Cubbin clay with lime, +5% gypsum, 5.0-6.0 pH, up to 8% calcium carbonate, 13% sodium silicate, up to 50 g/liter of potassium silicate: S. schmidgenii (Hairy)

- 2010: Apple releases the iPad and Google releases the Nexus One and iPhone 4S.

1. Stop blaming yourself and blaming others at the same time.  If you’re feeling guilty, it’s probably because you feel responsibility for what happened.  But don’t feel like you have to blame yourself for doing or saying something stupid.  Try to see people for their actions and reactions, and not for who is to blame.  Also, it may help to remember that people can’t control everything in life.  Don’t feel like you can control the course of events or other people’s decisions.

2. Stop feeling so responsible.  Feelings like guilt are often the result of feeling like you have to do everything right, or take responsibility for other people’s actions.  This is a kind of overreaction to the situation.  What happens in your story is your own fault, not someone else’s. In the US, for example, the cotton is typically harvested by a specialized group of people who farm the cotton upland region.  They plant the cotton, tend it, harvest it and process it. 

In some places of the world cotton is still harvested by hand but the systems used to process it are generally quite different.  For example most of the cotton that’s grown in Vietnam comes from the lowlands of southern Vietnam, so it’s generally grown in small fields and tended by families of men and women.  There is no processing involved, and often there is no washing of the cotton at all.  Since cotton is such an important crop at this time of year in Vietnam, families often make sure they plant the most cotton possible in their fields.

Another part of the world where cotton is sometimes harvested by hand is India.  In India the cotton harvesting process is done very much along the lines of the Vietnamese approach.  The different states in India are very diverse in terms of their climate and geography.  In some parts of India the farmers will take their cotton up to the hills and leave it down the foothills until the harvest time.  
However in India cotton is quite often harvested by hand.  In some areas it is very hard to get the cotton off the plant and the farmers will sometimes use their tractor or oxen to drag it from the plants. In some areas people can even pick the cotton by hand!

In parts of India where it is difficult to get the cotton off the plants, the farmers sometimes create a row of cotton that has been tied together, and then pull the cotton one piece at a time.  
Other parts of India have more modern planters that can be pulled behind a tractor.  

One other area of the world that may use more mechanization of some kind is Pakistan.  

This part of the world has one of the highest levels of income in the world, but it also has some of the lowest living standards.  
In Pakistan cotton is grown by small family farms in two parts of the country, the province of Punjab and the Sindh province.  In Punjab, in some areas of the cotton fields are linked together so that when the cotton is ready to harvest each farmer takes the cotton from one end to the other to pick it. 
For most parts of this region this method of picking cotton is quite effective.  In some parts of the region it means that people can afford to purchase farming equipment. However in many other parts the farming community, where most of the farmers live, do not have access to any farming equipment at all. 
For example, if a farmer needs to get the cotton off the plant one piece at a time, they have to wait until it rains for a couple of days until the cotton is loosened up and there is little chance of getting it with the help of a tractor or oxen. If the weather is dry, the cotton is very likely to be left growing in the next crop. 
In these areas, farming is often the only way to provide food.  

Finally, cotton harvesting in parts of Africa is done very much by hand.  In some areas in Africa there are fields in the fields that aren’t planted to cotton but are planted to corn and other crops.  When this corn crop is about to die back down to nothing, farmers often bring all of the cotton plants back together and pick it off one by one.

prompt: Human: How does water therapy work?
response:
Well, Water therapy is a type of physical therapy that uses water to improve function and mobility in people who have suffered some sort of injury or disability. It often involves exercises that are done in or near water. There are actually three main areas in which water therapy are used: swimming, water aerobics, and hot tub and underwater massage therapy. 

In swimming, people learn to use their arms and legs effectively as they perform water exercises such as freestyle, breaststroke, and sidestroke. They learn to kick and swim in the water comfortably and to control their breath and body position so that they can swim efficiently. The benefits of swimming are that it is a full body workout, very efficient, doesn’t hurt if someone is learning to swim, has a lower impact on the joints than running or cycling, and doesn’t tire the muscles of the legs as much as running and cycling. Swimming reduces joint and muscle pain, improves circulation and blood flow to the whole body, improves respiration, and maintains muscular strength and endurance. People usually find that they need less water to run or cycle after starting swimming or hot tub use.

For people who suffer from joint pain and have trouble moving while getting out of water, water aerobics is an excellent choice. To make exercising more comfortable, it is important that people use water, which can be made to flow in a very gentle way, and is also very soft. The most common aerobic exercises that take place in a water pool are buoyancy (where people do exercises in the water) and walking on water (a bit like floating in a pool or jacuzzi). This helps people to move in the water, get used to the way their body moves in the water, and learn to use water to exercise, so they can do many different kinds of exercises. 

Water is also used as part of the treatment of many conditions, such as muscle soreness, joint pain, fibromyalgia and chronic fatigue. Water also works with the body to recover from and heal injuries. Many medical conditions are made worse by sitting still. 

Hot tub and underwater massage therapy is more of a holistic form of therapy that combines massage and relaxation with the warmth of the water. Some people who are involved with hot tub therapy feel that it helps them feel relaxed and also increases the flow of positive energy throughout the body. The massage therapists use warm water, to help people relax and to have their muscles relaxed. Water, especially warm water can help the body to maintain the state of calm, which reduces anxiety, stress and pain.

There are a few things to be aware of, however. People who are not used to swimming, or to exercising in the water, can sometimes feel cold and find it difficult to warm up to the water. This usually improves as time goes on and people get used to it. It is important that people listen to their bodies and not over exert themselves. 

The water can become very cold at the beginning of the treatment, when one first starts out exercising in or near the water, and people can feel very cold and shiver. This can be painful and it can be hard to concentrate on doing the exercises. Some people prefer to do just the exercises in a hot tub or a Jacuzzi. These may be better, because they can be warmer and there is less risk of hurting oneself.  

Another thing to bear in mind is that one cannot use water therapy as an alternative to other types of physical therapy. Water therapy is different, but very useful for lots of different conditions. But the way you use water depends on the goal of your therapy, and one way might not work well in another. 

Water therapy is best done together with other treatments, perhaps with swimming, or with a therapist who can modify the exercises in an individualized way to fit each person’s needs. If you are someone who has had problems in or around your joints or with your muscles and/or who have trouble getting out of the water, it might be good to talk with a therapist who is interested in doing water therapy together with you. Another advantage to water therapy is that you can stay dry when you get out of the water, but if you have trouble using your arms or legs as you get out, it can be hard to remove your clothes, and sometimes clothing must stay on while you are doing exercises in or around the water.

Lastly, I should mention that there are some environmental and social barriers to water therapy. The more places that offer hot tubs or water therapy, the better. For lots of people this means that they can get out in the water instead of just staying inside. Bourekas

1 cup (8 oz.) firm or extra-firm tofu, cubed

2 tablespoons olive oil

2 cloves garlic, minced

2 tablespoons fresh thyme leaves, plus more to garnish

1 cup (15 oz.) small sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed

1 cup (8 oz.) baby carrots, peeled and cubed

1 cup (8 oz.) corn kernels (fresh or frozen)

4 cups (12 oz.) coarsely grated parmesan cheese

4 tablespoons fresh lemon juice

Salt and pepper

Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).

Meanwhile, in large skillet over medium heat, sauté potatoes, carrots, and corn until tender, about 2 minutes. Then add parmesan and lemon juice and stir to combine with vegetables, about 1 minute longer.

Divide evenly among four oven-safe serving dishes.

Pour topping evenly on each serving dish.

Bake until topping is golden, 10 to 15 minutes longer.

Serve immediately with extra thyme for garnish, if desired.
